claim: The palette row a surface is drawn with is clamp(shade + visibility-distance term, 0, numshades-1). A shade below 0 looks the same as 0 up close; it only resists darkening with distance. Blood's NORMAL.PLU is linear, about 1/64 of the texel's brightness per shade (100/88/75/63/50/38/25% at 0/8/16/24/32/40/48; 63 is black), and at visibility 800 distance adds about 1.2 shades per 1024 units (+13 at 8k, +38 at 32k).
evidence: Table and distance term measured from the game's own PAL/PLU in BLOOD.RFF by bloodmap/shade_table.py (2026-11-20).

bloodmap/sunlight.py: Blood's facade tiles are dark and busy (mean 39-67 of 255 at shade 0, texel spread 12-34), so a step under about 10-12 shades does not show on them; a blind reader called a shade-8 facade step 'nearly identical'
use: Choose shade steps with shade_table.brightness(tile, shade), not by number. On a facade a light step must be 10-20 shades to show.
